articles.title: Los 40 de Toni Bou causan el asombro y admiración de Marc Márquez, Iniesta, Guardiola, Sainz, Stoner, Jorge Martín...
articles.standfirst: Muchas estrellas deportivas de diversa índole elogian al 40 veces campeón mundial de Trial
articles.summary: Muchas estrellas deportivas de diversa índole elogian al 40 veces campeón mundial de Trial
articles.body: Toni Bou es, sin lugar a dudas, el personaje del fin de semana en lo que respecta al ámbito deportivo. El catalán ha sumado en Zelhem (Países Bajos) su cuadragésimo título consecutivo de campeón del mundo de Trial. Veinte pertenecen a la disciplina al aire libre y otros veinte corresponden al que se disputa bajo techo. El caso es que el piloto del Repsol Honda HRC es una figura que trasciende su nicho. Es una indiscutible estrella por el mero hecho de llevar ganando de forma ininterrumpida desde 2007. El insaciable competidor nacido en Piera (Barcelona) el 17 de octubre de 1986 está a una distancia sideral del segundo con más entorchados (el británico Dougie Lampkin, con 12 títulos mundiales y 135 victorias en pruebas del campeonato). Bou está muy por encima con esos 40 títulos y 274 globales. Y, por esta razón, muchos deportistas han mostrado públicamente su admiración. En un vídeo difundido por HRC se ve a múltiples estrellas ensalzar la figura del GOAT del Trial. El primero en congratularse del nuevo título de Bou ha sido Marc Márquez. De todos es bien sabido que mantienen una bonita amistad y eso se percibe en los jocosos comentarios del nueve veces campeón mundial. "1, 2, 3... 40. ¿Dónde vas, tío? Eres una bestia, una máquina. Muchas felicidades, disfruta. Eres todo un referente a seguir", indica el crack de Cervera. También ha irrumpido en escena Andrés Iniesta. El héroe de la primera estrella mundialista de la selección española de fútbol, materializada en 2010, se ha explayado tras conocerse el hito histórico. "Toni, felicidades por el nuevo título, no sólo por ganarlo, sino también por todo el esfuerzo y duro trabajo que hay detrás. Has pasado por momentos buenos y no tan buenos y ahí sigues al pie del cañón después de tantos años y ahí radica la dificultad de lo que has conseguido", indica el maravilloso centrocampista que brilló con luz propia en el mejor Barcelona de la historia. Luego nos hemos encontrado con una agradable sorpresa. Pep Guardiola también se ha sumado a esta ristra de loas. "Tony, soy el Pep. ¿No te da vergüenza? 40 campeonatos mundiales. ¡Has ganado 40 campeonatos mundiales! Es algo que ni en el mejor de los sueños se puede concebir. ¡Felicidades por la trayectoria, por la consistencia! Porque, escucha, aunque tu deporte no sea tan famoso como el fútbol, pero para ganar 40 títulos tienes que picar mucha piedra cada día. ¡Así que muchas felicidades! ¡Celebra este hito con los tuyos! Sólo puedo expresar toda la admiración del mundo. Un fuerte abrazo", subraya el laureado entrenador de Barça, Bayern y Manchester City. Volviendo al deporte de las dos ruedas, nos encontramos con otra leyenda agasajando al GOAT del Trial. Hablamos de Casey Stoner, bicampeón de la clase reina del Mundial de motociclismo. "Tony, seguro que sabes lo que estoy pensando. Pero, en verdad, es increíble lo que has conseguido. Durante los últimos 20 años, ha sido una cosa de locos tu dominio. 40 campeonatos mundiales. Indoor, outdoor, no importa las condiciones, no importa el día. Te levantas, actúas, un día sí y otro también rindes. Sinceramente, es un logro sin parangón. El resto sólo podemos soñar con hacer algo así. Así que muchas felicidades y disfrútalo como se merece", ha pormenorizado el australiano. Mientras, Jeffrey Herlings, que este domingo ha sellado su tricampeonato mundial de MXGP (sexto si se suman los tres de MX2) ha indicado: "¡Esos son números increíbles! ¡Gran felicidades por eso, hombre! ¡Es... Bueno, nunca he conocido a nadie con tantos campeonatos mundiales. ¡Es realmente algo especial! ¡Disfrútalo! ¡Y buena suerte para que ganes tu 41º! Probablemente llegará pronto...". Laia Sanz también está en la nómina de estrellas del deporte que han rendido tributo al de Piera. "Es brutal lo que ha conseguido. El hecho de que hayas ganado tanto puede hacer que parezca fácil, pero es increíble. Es histórico. No creo que haya nacido nadie que pueda ganarte. Espero que tardes muchos años en cansarte y que sigas ganando muchos más títulos. Eres uno de los mejores deportistas no sólo del Motor, sino de la historia", ha enfatizado la 14 veces campeona del mundo de Trial. Por su parte, Dani Pedrosa, tricampeón mundial y ganador de 54 carreras mundialistas, ha proclamado: "Toni, muchas felicidades por este impresionante 40º título. ¿Qué puedo decir? Sólo puedo expresar mi admiración. Esto no se había visto nunca antes en la historia del deporte, así que eres el número uno". Otro multicampeón (Joan Mir) ha ido en la misma línea que el resto: "¡Enhorabuena, Toni! Eres una inspiración para todos nosotros. 40 títulos es algo inimaginable. Si alguien lo podía conseguir, ése eras tú". Del mundo de las cuatro ruedas ha emergido Carlos Sainz Sr. "Me quiero sumar a todos los que te felicitan por este logro increíble. Enhorabuena y a disfrutarlo", ha afirmado el bicampeón mundial de rallies y tetracampeón del Dakar. Otra figura asociada al rally más exigente del mundo como es Cristina Gutiérrez ha afirmado: "Tengo la suerte de conocerte como persona estos últimos años y la verdad es que si ya te admiraba como deportista, ahora encima te admiro como persona. Me encanta esa capacidad de superación y esa motivación constante que tienes para conseguir lo que has conseguido. Nos inspiras muchísimo a todos y te mando un fuerte abrazo y que lo disfrutes". "¿40? Se dice rápido, es increíble, Toni eres incansable. ¡Disfrútalo mucho y con muchas ganas de que llegue el 41!", ha deseado Aleix Espargaró. Y Jorge Prado, dos veces campeón de MXGP y también bicampeón de MX2, ha soltado. "¿Qué pasa, Toni? Muchísimas felicidades por ese cuadragésimo título. La verdad que lo tuyo no es de este planeta. Gracias por hacernos disfrutar a todos los amantes del Trial de tu pilotaje". Fabio Quartararo ha bromeado con la gesta de Bou. "No sabía que se podía tener más títulos que años, pero te felicito y nos vemos en Andorra", ha dicho el que fuera campeón de MotoGP en 2021. Y de campeón a campeón. "Eres una inspiración para todos los deportistas jóvenes. Es un orgullo conocerte. Y con muchas ganas de que sigas sumando más", ha espetado Jorge Martín. Y con su gracejo habitual Pedro Acosta ha asegurado: "Felicidades Toni por tu campeonato número 40. A ver si dejas algo para los demás, macho, que con esto no se puede competir". Finalmente, el multicampeón Jordi Tarrés, predecesor de Bou, ha abrochado con una frase lapidaria: "¿40 títulos? ¡Guau! Es una cosa increíble. Yo creo que es un récord insuperable".

articles.title: Russell pone el asterisco al éxtasis de Antonelli: "A mí también me hubiese gustado parar"
articles.standfirst: Mercedes celebra un doblete perfecto y otro golpe a la F1, pero el británico sigue perdiendo opciones conforme pasan las carreras
articles.summary: Mercedes celebra un doblete perfecto y otro golpe a la F1, pero el británico sigue perdiendo opciones conforme pasan las carreras
articles.body: Y Monza estalló. Lo hace con poco que celebrar, pues si hay motivos es la mayor concentración de emociones que la Fórmula 1 puede reunir. Los tifosi invadían la recta principal, agitaban sus banderas de Italia y una sonrisa emergía en los hombros del pueblo con un fuerte olor a champán. No es otro que Kimi Antonelli, el vencedor en el Templo de la Velocidad tras la carrera que le encumbra definitivamente. Salió 19º, en 16 vueltas ya lideraba... y ganó. El Mundial sigue construyéndose piedra a piedra. "Es el mejor día de mi vida", resumía Kimi. Que en Monza encontró a sus primeros críticos tras destrozar su primer entrenamiento oficial con Mercedes las barreras de la Parabólica. Y allí cayó a lo más bajo en un 2025 donde se rumoreaba que si iban a cederle. 12 meses han bastado para que ya descuente días hasta ser campeón del mundo. "No quiero hablar del Mundial porque hemos visto lo rápido que cambian las cosas este año. Yo me lo tomo carrera a carrera, maximizo los resultados y las oportunidades. Después veré lo que pasa a final de año", explicó. Pero la diferencia crece. Ya en 66 puntos tras adelantar a Russell y romper el buen fin de semana del británico. "No tiene sentido que piense en el título, es mejor vivir en el momento, en el presente", añadió. Es rápido, el nuevo motor era imparable y Mercedes también decidió. Ahí llega el único asterisco que se puede poner. Que en F1 los hay de todos los colores y deben valorarse en su justa medida. Y la carrera los tiene desde la bandera roja por el choque de Leclerc hasta una degradación que tendió al cero. Pero Mercedes se cubrió con Antonelli y Russell tuvo que terminar con un duro en las lonas. "Primero debo felicitarle, pero creo que el equipo no sabía qué estrategia era buena y como Max [Verstappen] estaba en la pelea, decidieron partirlas. Quizá era lo correcto", expresó. Pero suena extraño que el líder de carrera no sea el que primero tiene la preferencia. Ahí llega el lío. "Me hubiese gustado parar. Y es fácil decir que hubiese ganado con la parada. Me hubiese gustado pelear con Kimi, pero probablemente hay otra razón en el equipo para tomar diferentes estrategias", puntualizó. Mercedes aumentó su mando y su líder, que es Antonelli, da un salto más. Eso sí, hay voces que lo critican. "Russell tiene que sentarse con el equipo y discutir lo que ocurrió. Estaba liderando, ¿por qué no tenía la opción de la parada gratis", analizó Martin Brundle, piloto noventero y comentarista de Sky. "Era la oportunidad de George para hacer algo en clave campeonato... y la distancia ha crecido", cerró.

articles.title: Daryz warms up for Arc with dominant display in Prix Foy
articles.summary: Daryz was given the perfect rehearsal ahead of his bid to retain his crown in the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe with a smooth success in the Prix Foy at Parislongchamp
articles.body:
Francis-Henri Graffard's charge made the perfect start to his four-year-old campaign by winning two more Group Ones at his beloved ParisLongchamp, with a comeback victory in the Prix Ganay followed by a runaway triumph in the Prix Aga Khan IV.

He could only finish third when sent across the Channel for the Prince of Wales's Stakes at Royal Ascot in June, but with connections feeling they had viable excuses for that below-par run, the son of Sea The Stars was expected to regain winning ways back on home turf.

On paper his task was not entirely straightforward, with George Scott's 10-length Coronation Cup winner and fellow Arc aspirant Bay City Roller among his three rivals, and as expected the latter was sent straight to the front by Oisin Murphy in an attempt to draw the sting out of Daryz's exceptional finishing kick.

But Mickael Barzalona always looked ultra-confident in the saddle aboard the red-hot favourite, who cruised alongside Bay City Roller a furlong out and only had to be pushed out hands and heels to win by a length and three-quarters.

"I couldn't be happier with the trial he had today. We got a good lead and luckily Oisin made the pace a little bit harder at the top of the hill, so the horse was really travelling nicely," Graffard told Sky Sports Racing.

"For me as a trainer it was the best preparation I could have for the horse. He will come on a lot for that, I left plenty in him, so he should be spot-on for four weeks' time."

Scott too was delighted with the performance of the runner-up and is hoping for rain in Paris ahead of a rematch with Daryz in Europe's premier middle-distance contest on October 4.

He said: "Oisin was very happy with him and we'll be hoping for a different set of circumstances in a month's time.

"We know that this horse has a high level of form on ground like this, but when it rains he's a different animal.

"He came here and travelled well, went through the race very well and got beaten by a better horse on the day. In four weeks' time that might be the case (again), but it might not, so we'll see.

"I think he's the best version of himself now. The winner might be as well, but in four weeks' time it's going to be completely different.

"He's going to be an underdog coming back, of course he is - Daryz is a champion and he is unbelievable around here. It was all perfect for him today and set up great, but I was very happy with our horse, Oisin was most happy, so we're looking forward to it."

Avec Toi made to work hard to stay unbeaten in Prix la Rochette

Hot favourite Avec Toi was made to pull out all the stops to maintain his unbeaten record in the Qatar Prix la Rochette at ParisLongchamp.

Christopher Head's colt had been hugely impressive in winning his first three starts and was long odds-on to make it four from four in this Group Three contest.

Imperial Strike, winner of his two previous starts for Andre and Lavinia Fabre, made a real race of it and there was little to choose between the pair in the dying strides, but Avec Toi was a short head in front at the line.

A likely rematch between the front two will take place in the Prix Jean-Luc Lagardere in four weeks' time.

Head told Sky Sports Racing: "It was a very nice race with five nice horses. I respected Imperial Strike from the beginning, so I'm very happy our horse won the race and we discovered there's a very nice horse to beat next time too!

"He's a very nice horse and he's done a great job today. It was a pretty tactical race and we are all happy.

"There is a lot to do between the two races and I'm very happy with that."

Ed Bethell's British raider Rogue Passion flashed home to claim Group Two honours in the Qatar Prix d'Aumale.

The Sioux Nation filly faced a significant step up in class having opened her account at the third time of asking at Carlisle three weeks ago.

Francis-Henri Graffard's Amusingly looked likely to win comfortably after travelling powerfully into the lead under Colin Keane, but Rossa Ryan produced Rogue Passion with a well-timed challenge to get up and claim victory.

Bethell told the Press Association: "We were hoping that she'd run a big race, she's a very nice filly who I've got a lot of time for.

"Obviously you don't know what you're taking on with the French horses, but she quickened up like a decent filly over the mile there and we're delighted."

When asked whether she would return to Paris for the Prix Marcel Boussac next month, the trainer added: "It's a conversation that needs to be had with the guys at Rogues Gallery (owners) because she needs to be supplemented if we're going to do it.

"We'll let the dust settle today, enjoy it and have the conversation in a few days' time. She's got options, but now she's a Group Two winner we want to try and get a Group One if we can.

"Today definitely was not unexpected. She's always shown she's a nice filly and it's a huge credit to the Rogues Gallery and Henry Lascelles who bought her."

articles.title: Erdenali shines at top table to claim Prix du Moulin honours
articles.summary: Erdenali headlined a winning day for the Aga Khan Stud with a scintillating display in the Group One Prix du Moulin at Parislongchamp, supported by successes from Varandir and stable star Daryz
articles.body:
A strong British and Irish contingent went to post for the Group One contest, with Aidan O'Brien's Irish 2,000 Guineas hero Gstaad the hot favourite ahead of Charlie Appleby's Opera Ballo and the Ed Walker-trained Ten Bob Tony.

Unlike that trio, Francis-Henri Graffard's Erdenali was unproven in Group One company, but he had looked an exciting prospect in winning his first three starts and was an unlucky loser when third in a Group Three on his most recent outing.

With Opera Ballo taken on for the lead by Gstaad's pacemaker Dorset, Appleby's charge was a spent force entering the final furlong, at which stage Erdenali and the shock Queen Anne winner Ten Bob Tony moved up to dispute the lead.

Erdenali was always getting the better of that particular battle, however, and the pair drew clear of Gstaad, who never threatened to land a telling blow and was ultimately a bit disappointing in third.

Nemone Routh, French racing manager and director for winning owners Aga Khan Studs, told Sky Sports Racing: "We were wondering if he was going to the Arc sale or not after this, but I don't think we will now!

"He's not a horse that shows very much in the morning - if you'd seen him work this week you wouldn't have been particularly impressed, but it all comes together in the afternoon.

"He should have been unbeaten - he should have won that Group Three very easily, we had just a nightmare trip.

"It was always the plan to come here; we needed to find out if he was a Group One horse and I think he's done that quite resoundingly."

Erdenali is Coral's new 2-1 favourite for the Queen Elizabeth II Stakes on Champions Day at Ascot, but with connections fortunate enough to have several horses in the same division, plans are on hold for the time being.

"We have some other horses for the Prix de la Foret - we have Samangan if the ground doesn't get too soft and we have Rayif, who might go to the QEII," Routh added.

"I think Erdenali is in the QEII as well and we were thinking of taking him to Keeneland for a race after this, but we might have to rethink now.

"He's definitely shown us he's a Group One horse."

Walker said of the runner-up Ten Bob Tony: "Thrilled, very proud of him again. I've slightly lost my voice.

"He's amazing and he's had an amazing season. He's really stepped it up a gear, it was a huge run. I'm kind of a bit gutted as I thought we had it. I saw we had Opera Ballo and Gstaad beat and probably didn't give the winner the respect he deserves - he looks very good and we were probably beaten by a very good horse.

"The plan was always the QEII. Whether we do the QEII and the Breeders' Cup, we'll see. We'll do what's right by him, hopefully he'll be around for many more years."

Benvenuto Cellini disappoints as Varandir secures Prix Niel glory

Irish Derby hero Benvenuto Cellini proved bitterly disappointing as Varandir claimed a decisive victory in the Qatar Prix Niel at ParisLongchamp.

Down the field as favourite for the Derby at Epsom before controversially being declared a non-runner due to an incident in the starting stalls, Benvenuto Cellini bounced back to claim Classic glory at the Curragh three weeks later, since when he had finished a creditable third against his elders in the King George at Ascot.

Returning from a short break, the son of Frankel was widely expected to stake his claim for the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe over the same course and distance in four weeks' time, but after going in pursuit of his pacesetting stablemate Montreal from the home turn, he found little for pressure and weakened into fifth place.

With Montreal's petrol tank running on empty entering the final furlong, having streaked clear of his rivals for much of the race, Francis-Henri Graffard's Varandir - a close-up fourth behind the William Haggas-trained Maltese Cross in the Grand Prix de Paris on his last outing - was the one who finished best to grab the lead under Mickael Barzalona and he was ultimately a comfortable winner over the staying-on Alam.

When asked whether the victory was a surprise, Nemone Routh, French racing manager and director for winning owners Aga Khan Studs, told Sky Sports Racing: "No, not hugely. We knew the horse was really well, we knew he'd progressed a lot and we were very happy with his run in the Grand Prix de Paris - he really moved forward from when he won the Group Three and I think he'd moved forward a lot since then.

"He's a horse that mentally and physically has improved throughout the year and we knew we had him well. I think he needed this run, because he was a bit heavy in the preliminaries."

Coral cut Varandir for 20-1 from 40-1 for the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe and while the same connections have last year's winner Daryz set to defend his crown, this son of Zarak is clearly entitled to line up alongside him.

Routh added: "He is in the Arc. We obviously need to speak to Princess Zahra (owner), (but) I'd say why not run? That would be my idea right now.

"I think he goes on any ground and sometimes it's good to have two runners as you can be drawn 18 out of 18 with one and have a good draw with another, so why not spread your chances? It's a possibility."

articles.title: Friendly Soul makes all to strike in Prix Vermeille
articles.summary: Friendly Soul delivered a breathtaking performance in the Prix Vermeille, kicking clear from some way out and lasting out gamely for a second Group One success.
articles.body:
A top-level winner in the Prix de l'Opera on Arc weekend two years ago, John and Thady Gosden's five-year-old missed the entirety of last season through injury.

However, she has slowly come to the boil in three starts this term, most recently chasing home Diamond Necklace in the Nassau Stakes at Goodwood.

And although she was tackling a mile and a half for the first time on her return to France, jockey James Doyle did not appear to have any stamina doubts, sending his mount straight to the lead from the off.

Friendly Soul and Composing had built up a healthy lead over the chasing pack rounding the home turn and while both Pink Panthera and Sunly came from further back to mount a late challenge - with the latter perhaps an unlucky loser after missing the break and encountering traffic problems in the straight - the Gosden runner had enough in hand to claim victory.

"It was a hugely sporting decision from her owners, George and Julia Strawbridge, to keep her in training at this age," Thady Gosden told Sky Sports Racing.

"Last time she was here she won the Prix de l'Opera, a couple of years ago now. She likes to do things her own way and took James to the front there, but she didn't get an easy lead at all - she got attacked in the false straight there and was never really able to get a breather.

"Obviously she's a hugely talented filly and very tough too. It's great to have her back to her best."

Friendly Soul is a 16-1 shot for the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe with Coral. When asked whether Europe's premier middle-distance contest could now be on the agenda, Gosden added: "It was obviously her first time over a mile and a half, so it was slightly unknown territory before this.

"I haven't had a chance to speak to George and Julia yet, we'll see how she comes out of the race and see where they'd like to go with her, but of course it's great to have it (Arc) as an option."

articles.title: Italian GP: Did Mercedes strategy cost George Russell win at Monza against Kimi Antonelli?
articles.summary: George Russell was overtaken late on by Kimi Antonelli after the latter caught his team-mate on an alternative strategy after pitting under a Virtual Safety Car; watch every session of the Spanish Grand Prix at a new track in Madrid from this Friday, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
Russell led Antonelli, who stormed through the field from 19th to be in the lead battle after just 13 laps, by one second when a race-changing Virtual Safety Car was called with 25 laps remaining.

Mercedes pitted Antonelli, but not Russell, for new medium tyres, which put the team-mates 15 seconds apart when the VSC ended.

From sixth, Antonelli overtook his rivals one by one then caught and overtook Russell with three laps to go to win his home event.

It leaves Russell 66 points behind Antonelli in the Drivers' Championship with 10 rounds to go.

"I was on the hard tyre and Kimi was on the medium tyre [when the VSC came], so if either of us were to pit, it was going to be Kimi," said Russell.

"I guess, why I was just a little bit annoyed with the timing of that VSC because, like Max said, I think it would have been tough for those guys on the medium to have competed with anybody on the hard tyre. But, it takes nothing away from Kimi's drive altogether."

Had Mercedes pitted both drivers, Antonelli would have been stuck behind for a few seconds in the pit lane, therefore losing track position to Max Verstappen, who also pitted under the VSC.

Russell told Sky Sports F1 : "The VSC came at an awkward time. I don't think the team knew what the right strategy was and, as Max was in the fight, decided to split the strategy which was probably the right thing for the team to do.

"In hindsight of course, it's easy to say I should have pitted or, if I won the race, they would have said Kimi should have stayed out.

"I would have liked to have had a fight with Kimi. It was quite a nice battle and I felt I was holding my own at that point. That was probably another reason the team wanted us to go on a different strategy. I get it."

Wolff explains Mercedes' thinking at time of VSC

Toto Wolff revealed Mercedes' computer systems told them, at the time of the VSC, that Russell's strategy would be faster than Antonelli's with the Italian expected to "come close but wouldn't catch".

Mercedes believed the hard tyre was a "forever tyre" that would effectively last the whole race, but not with the performance of the medium.

"The differentiator today was the ability going through the traffic [from Antonelli]. We've seen it with other great ones in the past. Lewis [Hamilton] put it in some of the races and that's what he's shown today," said Wolff.

"There's just no stopping when a driver and a car are one, then there's nothing that can stop them."

Coming into the weekend, Antonelli was expected to lose points to his closest title rivals - Russell, Lewis Hamilton and Lando Norris.

Instead, he's extended his advantage and Russell is set to start at the back himself in one of the upcoming races as he does not have enough engines to finish the season without a grid penalty.

However, Russell says he's "not thinking about" the title race and instead is looking at the positives of being competitive in Monza and Zandvoort compared to the events before the summer break.

"We are where we are. Kimi's been driving incredibly this season and deserves to be leading the championship and he's got a healthy lead," he said.

"I'm not going to think about the fight or the comeback. I'm just thinking about going to every race and trying to win it. It will be what it will be. I'm not putting any pressure on myself in this regard, saying 'I need to do this or that'. I just need to win more races and, of course, he's in this spot."
